messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Triggers → Threat
  - Triggers → Memory
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Threat
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Memory → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory → Negative Appraisals
  - Threat → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Memory
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Threat

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Mr. Tran, a 66-year-old South Eastern Asian man, has been a roofer for over three decades. Recently, his life took an unexpected turn when he was exposed to toxic chemicals during a workplace accident. Since that fateful day, Mr. Tran’s daily routine and mental health have spiraled into a chaotic and distressing cycle. The incident occurred late one afternoon as he was working on the roof of a commercial building. A nearby tank containing hazardous chemicals exploded, releasing a thick cloud of noxious gas that enveloped him instantly. As he inhaled deeply to catch his breath, Mr. Tran felt a sharp burning sensation in his lungs and a wave of dizziness washed over him. He managed to stagger away from the site but was overwhelmed by the lingering antiseptic smell long after he had left. Since then, nighttime has become particularly daunting for Mr. Tran. The darkness seems to amplify his fears and triggers vivid memories of that day. Every time he wakes up in the dark, the suffocating sensation returns, and he is transported back to the moment when he felt trapped by the toxic fumes. This intense replay of the traumatic event has made it nearly impossible for him to sleep soundly or feel truly relaxed even in a safe place. In his occupation as a roofer, Mr. Tran often encounters unfamiliar places where the risk of encountering similar dangers feels overwhelming. The memory of that terrifying explosion plays like a film over and over again in his mind. Sometimes, he experiences a surge of intense emotions without any clear image, which leaves him feeling disoriented and anxious. Mr. Tran has come to believe that he cannot rely on himself anymore. He fears that if something goes wrong, he won’t be able to handle it as effectively as before. This sense of hopelessness has deepened his conviction that the world is a dangerous place. The traumatic event has reshaped his perspective, making him hyper-vigilant and distrustful of both himself and the environment around him. In an attempt to cope with these overwhelming feelings, Mr. Tran has adopted several maladaptive strategies. He often dwells on how he used to be before the accident, comparing his current state unfavorably to who he was then. This past dwelling only intensifies his negative appraisals, reinforcing his sense of hopelessness and inability to rely on himself. Mr. Tran tries hard not to think about the trauma, but every time a trigger arises—whether it’s the darkness or an antiseptic smell—the memories flood back with vivid detail. He becomes consumed by thoughts of how he couldn’t prevent the accident and how helpless he felt in that moment. These intrusive memories are accompanied by an overwhelming sense of danger and threat, leading him to avoid any situations where he might feel vulnerable again. His maladaptive strategies have led him to become extremely reluctant to assert himself or disagree with others, fearing it could lead to conflict. This avoidance has strained his relationships, particularly with his wife, who feels increasingly isolated and concerned about his well-being. As Mr. Tran’s world narrows further due to these coping mechanisms, he finds himself trapped in a vicious cycle of triggers, memories, negative appraisals, and maladaptive strategies that feed into each other, tightening the noose around him. He has come to believe that his future is bleak, and this belief only exacerbates his symptoms. Finally, it was his wife’s persistent encouragement that brought Mr. Tran to seek help. She saw how much he had changed and urged him to find a way out of the darkness. What frightens him most now is the thought of continuing to live in such a state of fear and distress. He hopes for a chance to reclaim some semblance of normalcy, to feel safe again in his own skin, and to reconnect with the life he once led. The road ahead will be challenging, but Mr. Tran is willing to take the first step towards healing, hoping that through therapy, he can break free from this debilitating cycle and regain a sense of control over his life.
